mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate consistently signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines in the prior month but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has been above 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate and decline in non-farm payrolls signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending power and corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of instances (i.e., 60-day returns are positive in >40% of such cases).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), a rising federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY, FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in 1 month but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts reflects strong consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases in the prior month but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 100.0 for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that typically precedes a slowdown in economic growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO has been below 100.0 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation and decline in industrial production signals a stagflationary shock that increases corporate costs and reduces demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of CPIAUCSL rise and INDPRO decline fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of instances (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in >40% of such cases).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%), a decline in non-farm payrolls signals an unexpected labor market slowdown that typically leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0%, PAYEMS declines > 0.5% in 1 month but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.
